subject: Capacity debt alert — customer throughput lag & recovery plan
messages:
From: Anna Park <anna@quickpay.io>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.company, marissa_cole@redwood.company
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Persistent latency + errors impacting QuickPay checkout (prod)

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

We've seen sustained token-latency spikes and 5xx rates jump on our dedicated pool since ~02:30 PST this morning. Checkout requests are timing out for a subset of customers; our retries are increasing payment latency and some transactions are rerouted. We haven't changed client traffic patterns on our side.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's reserved capacity for our tenant or if there's ongoing work in the us-west region? We need visibility ASAP — this is affecting our SLAs and our ops team is receiving escalations.

Attaching a short snippet from our end showing 95p/99p latency and error traces.

Thanks,
Anna Park
Director, Platform Engineering
QuickPay

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.company
To: Anna Park <anna@quickpay.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.company, rishi_malhotra@redwood.company
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Persistent latency + errors impacting QuickPay checkout (prod)

Hi Anna — thanks for the heads up and the trace. We're pulling telemetry now. Initial checks show sustained queueing on QuickPay's reserved pool (pool id rp-43) coincident with a spike in long-sequence requests from a small subset of clients. No config changes from us in the past 48 hours.

Immediate plan:
- I'm escalating to engineering ops and our capacity team.
- We'll validate whether KV cache pressure or a slow model variant is causing longer token times.
- I will update you in 30 minutes with observed 95th/99th percentiles and a mitigation ETA.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize QuickPay.

—Mateo
Staff PM, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.company

Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.company
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:50:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Persistent latency + errors impacting QuickPay checkout (prod)

On Wed, Mar 3, 2027 at 09:25 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.company> wrote:
> Immediate plan:
> - I'm escalating to engineering ops and our capacity team.

I dug into serving metrics for rp-43. Key findings so far:
- 40% rise in average KV cache-miss rate over the last 2 hours.
- Long-seq tail dominated by a specific model variant (rwd-model-x-q4) for requests with >2k tokens.
- Autoscaler hasn't added nodes because reservation limits were reached (reserved_x: 16/16).

Short-term mitigation options (ranked):
1) Hotfix routing: divert new requests over a compatible, lower-latency quantized variant in the same model family for 15 minutes. Minimal risk, immediate effect.
2) Temporarily raise reserved node cap for QuickPay by +4 GPUs and allow burst (requires exec sign-off). Fast but impacts capacity pool budget.
3) Throttle long-sequence requests at the proxy and return a structured retry header (client change).

I'll prepare a short telemetry dump and recommended action. If we want to avoid customer-facing throttles, option 1 + quick node bump is my preference.

-Rishi
Senior Backend Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.company

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.company, rishi_malhotra@redwood.company, evelyn_hart@redwood.company, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.company
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 18:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Capacity debt alert — customer throughput lag & recovery plan

Anna — quick update and remediation summary for your ops and exec teams.

Timeline & root cause (short):
- 2027-03-03 02:18–03:40 PST: sudden rise in long-sequence traffic caused KV cache churn and a spike in model-x-q4 tail latency.
- Our reserved pool rp-43 hit its reserved node ceiling preventing autoscaler from adding capacity. This is the capacity-debt scenario — reservation limits + bursty long-sequence traffic.

What we did (mitigations):
- 03:00 PST: Applied hotfix routing to a lower-latency quantized variant for new long-sequence traffic (rwd-model-x-q4-fast). Immediate reduction in 99p latency from ~2.1s -> ~0.9s for affected requests.
- 03:15 PST: Vivek authorized emergency burst of +4 GPUs to rp-43 for 3 hours. Nodes were added and KV cache warmed; error rate returned to baseline within 25 minutes.
- 03:45 PST: We removed the temporary burst; autoscaler and cache behavior observed as stable.

Attached: pool_kv_cache_dump_20270304.csv, throughput-graph-0305.png, and the small routing patch applied.

Next steps (prevent recurrence):
- Short-term (2 weeks): implement routing-based per-tenant long-seq protection and conservative fallback variants for any long-sequence request >1.5k tokens.
- Mid-term (1–2 months): increase reserved headroom options for enterprise tenants and expose a self-serve burst API with pre-approved finance flags.
- Postmortem with QuickPay ops and a joint runbook for similar incidents.

We're sorry for the impact. We're scheduling a 30-minute post-incident call Tuesday to walk through telemetry and the runbook; I will send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Staff PM, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
